output.brief:
The rise in cancellations is mostly not a pricing problem. It comes from the Quillbook accounting connector. Quillbook retired its old invoice interface on 30 March. Since then the connector has silently dropped or duplicated invoices: 58,300 across 1,212 accounts. Of those accounts, 34% have cancelled, against 8% of Quillbook accounts with no recorded failure. Quillbook accounts churn at about 6% a month whether they are repriced or on the locked price. Accounts with no connector, which are most of the base, are barely changed (1.9% against 1.8%), including the largest seat band. The earlier link between bigger price increases and more cancellations is explained by the fact that bigger accounts are more likely to use Quillbook. The failures are logged only as warnings, so the health panel misses them. The ticket is rated low severity and has no schedule.

What to do next:
- Make the Quillbook fix (move to the new interface) the top engineering priority.
- Contact every Quillbook account, including those that cancelled, to correct their invoices.
- Do not reverse the price rise.
- Do not switch off the duplicate-invoice hold. It has kept 3,870 duplicates out of customers' books.
- Hold the Tallymarsh rebuild until its log has been reviewed. Its churn change is within normal variation.

I'm fairly confident in this. Support slowness is a probable secondary factor, but I haven't established it.
